items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: In the sense of like Steve Reich and Phillip Glass, but in a jazz context.

ctx.x: Periodic, yeah. In the sense of like Steve Reich and Phillip Glass, but in a jazz context. And it’s just using forms that subtract or add. Additive and subtractive forms. So I have a lot of pieces like that. Not much of it was recorded. We just did one with the Omi Orchestra called “Time Is.” So it goes Time is/Time is in/Time is in this/Time is in this if/Time is in this/Time is in/Time is time. So it’s like one, two, five, two, slip back in. And so sometimes — there was a whole period where I wrote a bunch of…
Do you ever write music that is specific to things happening in your small world or in the world as a whole?
